## Proof

**Setup.** Let $C_{ij}$ denote the cofactor of $a_{ij}$ in $A$. Replacing $a_{ij}$ by $2-a_{ij}$ changes the determinant by $(2-2a_{ij})\,C_{ij}$, so the hypothesis $\det(A)=\det(A_{ij})$ gives
$$
(1-a_{ij})\,C_{ij}=0 \qquad\text{for all } i,j. \tag{$\star$}
$$

**Key observation.** For each row index $j$, let $D_j$ be the determinant of the matrix obtained from $A$ by replacing row $j$ with the all-ones row $\mathbf{1}^T$. Expanding $D_j$ along row $j$ (the cofactors are unaffected by row $j$'s entries):
$$
D_j=\sum_{i=1}^n C_{ji}.
$$
Also $\det A = \sum_i a_{ji}\,C_{ji}$ (expansion along row $j$). Subtracting and using $(\star)$:
$$
D_j - \det A = \sum_{i=1}^n (1-a_{ji})\,C_{ji}=0.
$$
Hence
$$
D_j = \det A \qquad\text{for every } j. \tag{1}
$$

**Computing $\det B$.** Since $b_{ij}=a_{ij}+(-1)^i$, the matrix $B$ is the rank-one update
$$
B = A + \mathbf{c}\,\mathbf{1}^T, \qquad \mathbf{c}=((-1)^1,\dots,(-1)^n)^T,\quad \mathbf{1}=(1,\dots,1)^T.
$$
By the identity $\det(A+uv^T)=\det(A)+v^T\operatorname{adj}(A)\,u$ (the matrix-determinant lemma, valid for all $A$ by polynomiality),
$$
\det B = \det A + \mathbf{1}^T\operatorname{adj}(A)\,\mathbf{c}.
$$
Using $\operatorname{adj}(A)_{ij}=C_{ji}$,
$$
\mathbf{1}^T\operatorname{adj}(A)\,\mathbf{c}=\sum_{i,j}C_{ji}\,(-1)^j=\sum_{j=1}^n (-1)^j\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n C_{ji}\Bigr)=\sum_{j=1}^n (-1)^j D_j.
$$
Applying (1):
$$
\det B = \det A + \det A\sum_{j=1}^n (-1)^j.
$$

**Conclusion.** The alternating sum $\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^j$ equals $0$ when $n$ is even and $-1$ when $n$ is odd.

- If $n$ is even: $\det B=\det A$, so $\det B(\det A-\det B)=0$.
- If $n$ is odd: $\det B=\det A-\det A=0$, so $\det B(\det A-\det B)=0$.

In both cases,
$$
\boxed{\det B\,(\det A-\det B)=0}.
$$

## Proof

**Setup.** Let $C_{ij}$ denote the cofactor of $a_{ij}$ in $A$. Replacing $a_{ij}$ by $2-a_{ij}$ changes the determinant by $(2-2a_{ij})\,C_{ij}$, so the hypothesis $\det(A)=\det(A_{ij})$ gives
$$
(1-a_{ij})\,C_{ij}=0 \qquad\text{for all } i,j. \tag{$\star$}
$$

**Key observation.** For each row index $j$, let $D_j$ be the determinant of the matrix obtained from $A$ by replacing row $j$ with the all-ones row $\mathbf{1}^T$. Expanding $D_j$ along row $j$ (the cofactors are unaffected by row $j$'s entries):
$$
D_j=\sum_{i=1}^n C_{ji}.
$$
Also $\det A = \sum_i a_{ji}\,C_{ji}$ (expansion along row $j$). Subtracting and using $(\star)$:
$$
D_j - \det A = \sum_{i=1}^n (1-a_{ji})\,C_{ji}=0.
$$
Hence
$$
D_j = \det A \qquad\text{for every } j. \tag{1}
$$

**Computing $\det B$.** Since $b_{ij}=a_{ij}+(-1)^i$, the matrix $B$ is the rank-one update
$$
B = A + \mathbf{c}\,\mathbf{1}^T, \qquad \mathbf{c}=((-1)^1,\dots,(-1)^n)^T,\quad \mathbf{1}=(1,\dots,1)^T.
$$
By the identity $\det(A+uv^T)=\det(A)+v^T\operatorname{adj}(A)\,u$ (the matrix-determinant lemma, valid for all $A$ by polynomiality),
$$
\det B = \det A + \mathbf{1}^T\operatorname{adj}(A)\,\mathbf{c}.
$$
Using $\operatorname{adj}(A)_{ij}=C_{ji}$,
$$
\mathbf{1}^T\operatorname{adj}(A)\,\mathbf{c}=\sum_{i,j}C_{ji}\,(-1)^j=\sum_{j=1}^n (-1)^j\Bigl(\sum_{i=1}^n C_{ji}\Bigr)=\sum_{j=1}^n (-1)^j D_j.
$$
Applying (1):
$$
\det B = \det A + \det A\sum_{j=1}^n (-1)^j.
$$

**Conclusion.** The alternating sum $\sum_{j=1}^n(-1)^j$ equals $0$ when $n$ is even and $-1$ when $n$ is odd.

- If $n$ is even: $\det B=\det A$, so $\det B(\det A-\det B)=0$.
- If $n$ is odd: $\det B=\det A-\det A=0$, so $\det B(\det A-\det B)=0$.

In both cases,
$$
\boxed{\det B\,(\det A-\det B)=0}.
$$
